audit_findings.title: Post-year acquisition breaks perimeter and date coherence
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.011 million combined purchase consideration for PBC and Precision Design, equal to 0.33% of the $9,395 million base equity value and 0.46% of the $6,749 million bear equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The June 2026 cash and debt bridge includes the acquisition funding, while the FY2025 OE anchor excludes the acquired operations and their financing costs.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 2, 2026 , we completed the acquisition of Premium Building, a truss and wall panel products supplier, serving customers in eastern New York.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, but the latest filing establishes a small scale: both 2026 acquisitions together cost $31.011 million, and the company reported that they were not material to interim results individually or in aggregate. PBC alone is smaller than the stated combined amount. The direction remains unknown because the record does not separate PBC's earnings, financing costs, or purchase consideration.
audit_findings.action: Document PBC-specific purchase consideration, funding, post-interest OE and integration costs; correct the perimeter in the next routine valuation update rather than rerunning the present conclusion solely for this item.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-supported growth may be treated as free
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,123.328 million of 2025 acquisition cash outlay, equal to 12.0% of the $9,395 million base equity value; valuation error unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition-derived earnings can enter the OE anchor and forecast growth even though the purchase consideration is excluded from conventional OE and from forecast reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, we completed a number of acquisitions for a combined $ 1.1 billion purchase price, net of cash acquired, including the acquisitions of (i) Alpine Lumber, (ii) O.C. Cluss, (iii) Truckee Tahoe, (iv) St. George Truss, (v) Stately Las Vegas, (vi) Rystin, (vii) Lengefeld Lumber, and (viii) Pleasant Valley.
audit_findings.explanation: The substantial acquisition spending is demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether the 3%-5% forecast growth is organic or assumes continued acquisitions. If acquisitions are required, omitting their purchase capital would overstate distributable OE; if the forecast is wholly organic, there is no such error. The known capital scale is large enough to matter, but the valuation effect cannot be established without separating growth sources.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 and projected sales and OE into organic and acquired components, annualize acquired interest and earnings, and rerun any acquisition-supported growth case with purchase consideration charged at evidenced acquisition multiples.

audit_findings.title: Growth may omit required working-capital investment
audit_findings.magnitude: $184.251 million H1 2026 net cash use across the filed operating working-capital line items, equal to 27.7% of the $664 million OE anchor; normalized valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental inventory, receivables, contract assets and related liabilities reduce distributable OE or must be included in the reinvestment rate supporting growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The composition and level of working capital typically change during periods of increasing sales as we carry more inventory and receivables.
audit_findings.explanation: Working-capital cash demands are demonstrated, including a computed $184.251 million use in H1 2026, but that interim amount is seasonal and cannot be treated as normalized annual reinvestment. The record also does not show whether the stated 19.9% RONTA calculation includes normalized working capital. Omission could materially overstate OE, but neither omission nor its recurring magnitude is established.
audit_findings.action: Produce the RONTA numerator and denominator by component, confirm inclusion of normalized operating working capital, and rerun each growth case using a multi-year incremental working-capital-to-sales requirement if it is absent.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified litigation is a potential claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured settlements, deductibles and defense costs would reduce OE when paid or require a liability deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Although the Company cannot estimate a reasonable range of loss based on currently available information, the resolution of these matters could have a material adverse effect on the Company's financial position, results of operations or cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The claims and reasonable possibility of loss are demonstrated, but no loss range is estimable. Insurance reserves exist for broader insured risks, while the filings do not isolate construction-defect reserves, self-insured retention or uncovered exposure. The June 2026 filing retains potentially material contingency language but also states management's belief that currently pending or threatened claims will not materially affect consolidated results. The record therefore cannot establish valuation materiality.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent filings and claim-specific records for reserves, deductible and retention amounts, coverage limits, insurer disputes, settlement developments and any reasonably estimable uninsured exposure; then charge recurring claims to OE or deduct a one-time liability as appropriate.

audit_findings.title: The anchor embeds an unusually low tax rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.892 million of 2025 after-tax earnings versus applying the filed 22.3% 2024 rate to $512.382 million of pretax income; approximately $518 million or $4.63 per share in the base DCF if propagated through the same valuation path
audit_findings.mechanism: The 15.1% tax rate increases after-tax net income within the OE anchor, and growth of the unnormalized anchor carries that benefit through forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our effective tax rate was 15.1% in 2025, a decrease compared to the 22.3% in 2024, primarily related to the benefit of income tax credits, impact of state income taxes and discrete tax adjustments, partially offset by permanent differences, relative to a decreased income before income taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The unusually low 15.1% rate is demonstrated and includes credits, favorable state-tax effects and discrete adjustments. Using the prior-year 22.3% rate produces a $36.892 million anchor sensitivity, about 5.6% of OE and 5.5% of base equity value when propagated through the existing DCF. That is reasonably capable of affecting the valuation conclusion. The full amount is not proven to be an error because some credits may recur and enacted tax provisions are expected to reduce future cash taxes.
audit_findings.action: Separate recurring credits from discrete benefits and timing deferrals, establish a normalized cash-tax rate using filed tax components and 2026 guidance, and rerun the OE anchor and all scenarios with that rate.

audit_findings.title: Immediate growth may skip a flat 2026 operating environment
audit_findings.magnitude: H1 2026 operating income fell $350.705 million and net income fell $332.649 million year over year; OE valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An explicit weak 2026 path would reduce early forecast OE and its present value before the long-term growth and fade assumptions begin.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2026, the Industry Forecast Composite is forecasting U.S. total housing starts and U.S. single-family housing starts to remain relatively flat compared to 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is no longer only a forward-looking possibility. H1 2026 sales declined 9.4%, core organic sales declined 7.5%, gross margin fell from 30.6% to 28.2%, and operating income fell from $495.728 million to $145.023 million. Those filed results contradict immediate positive growth in the base and bull paths and show substantial operating deleverage. Owner earnings cannot be quantified from the supplied interim data alone, but the earnings deterioration is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a full-year 2026 OE estimate from filed year-to-date results, seasonality, working-capital normalization, taxes and acquisition effects, then rerun every scenario with an explicit 2026 transition year before applying long-term growth and fade assumptions.
